findings.title: Backup-code login skips the password when totpCode is set
findings.body: Password verification runs only when `user.password` is set and `credentials.totpCode` is empty (the check around line 121). The new backup-code branch then logs the user in if the backup code matches and never validates `totpCode`. A request with the victim's email, any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000"), and a valid backup code therefore skips the password entirely, consumes that code, and creates a session. Backup codes are supposed to replace the authenticator only; the login UI still sends the password and clears totpCode, but the credentials callback must not trust the client to omit totpCode. Anyone who obtains a backup code (the downloaded cal-backup-codes.txt, a screenshot, a clipboard history) can take over the account without the password. Verify the password inside this branch whenever the user has one, and do not treat an unchecked totpCode as proof the password was already accepted.

findings.title: One-time backup codes are consumed with a lost update
findings.body: Redeeming a backup code decrypts the stored list, finds a match, sets that slot to null, and writes the whole blob back with a plain user.update keyed only by id. There is no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-swap on the previous ciphertext. Two overlapping logins can both read the same list and both succeed: the same code opens two sessions, and if the requests use two different codes the later write restores the code the earlier request consumed. The promise that each code works exactly once is therefore not enforced. Consume the code with a conditional update (or SELECT FOR UPDATE) that fails if backupCodes changed, and only then issue the session.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive and unnormalized
findings.body: Codes are generated as lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex") in setup.ts) and login compares them with indexOf after only stripping "-". The same check is in apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts at the backupCode.replaceAll call. There is no toLowerCase() or trim, and spaces are left in place. The recovery input in apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx uses placeholder "XXXXX-XXXXX" and does not set autoCapitalize="none", so mobile keyboards and anyone following the placeholder submit uppercase hex. Those attempts always fail as an incorrect backup code, which blocks the recovery path when the authenticator is already lost. Normalize by trimming, removing dashes and spaces, and lowercasing on the server, and stop advertising uppercase in the field.

findings.title: Closing the codes dialog does not finish 2FA setup
findings.body: On a successful enable response the modal only moves to DisplayBackupCodes and no longer calls onEnable(). onEnable() runs solely from the footer Close button. Escape, the overlay, and the dialog's default close control go through onOpenChange and do not notify the parent, so the settings switch stays off while twoFactorEnabled is already true on the server. Clicking the switch again calls setup and gets TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled, so the user cannot finish or disable 2FA until a full reload. The codes themselves exist only in component state and a blob URL from the earlier setup response; nothing can fetch or regenerate them. Refreshing, closing the tab, or dismissing the dialog drops the only copy. The copy button makes this worse: navigator.clipboard.writeText is not awaited, and the success toast is shown even if the write fails, so the user can close thinking the codes were saved. Call onEnable() when enable succeeds (and on every close after that), require an explicit save acknowledgement, and do not toast success unless the clipboard write resolves.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes points at a settings flow that does not exist
findings.body: The new string says "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." This PR only creates codes inside the initial 2FA setup response and never adds a settings action to generate or rotate them. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration, or who dismissed the one-time codes screen, hit this error on "Lost access" and are told to do something the product cannot do. They can only get codes by disabling 2FA (which still requires the authenticator) and turning it on again. The message should not claim a generate-in-settings flow unless that flow exists.

findings.title: Tests never log in or disable 2FA with a backup code
findings.body: The new coverage only clicks download, copy, and close on the codes screen. Nothing submits a backup code at login, checks that a used code is rejected, or disables 2FA with a backup code (the TODO at the top of this file calls that out). The existing enable-and-login test was not updated for the new screen: after OTP it never clicks backup-codes-close, and expect(locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy() asserts on the Promise returned by isChecked(), which is always truthy, so it passes even when the switch is unchecked. A break in backup-code authentication, including the password bypass and the non-atomic consume, would not fail CI.
